Overview02 / 52

The direct store needs a clearer reason to buy

Atop already has distinctive inventory and an established marketplace reputation. The audit focuses on helping those strengths translate into direct website purchases.

What the business brings

  • Harmony Kingdom pieces from the former company archives.
  • Polish Pottery with recognizable makers, forms, and patterns.
  • Online selling experience since 2003, with personal service and careful packing.

What shoppers need

  • An obvious route to the right collection or exact item.
  • Clear item details, availability, and delivery expectations.
  • Confidence in the people handling a fragile or collectible purchase.

Category priorities: Harmony Kingdom Archives first, Polish Pottery second.

Competitor analysis10 / 52

The useful lessons are selective

Adapt for Atop

  1. Visible search and explicit collection routes.
  2. A small selection of available products with prices.
  3. Concise specifications and delivery reassurance.
  4. Related products with a clear reason to belong together.

Issues to avoid

Sold-out merchandising: Polish Pottery House’s bestseller view included several unavailable products near the start.

Conflicting offers: Outlet showed two different free-shipping gaps for the same basket.

Excess complexity: Large catalogs can justify navigation, loyalty, and registry features that Atop may not need.

Observed November 13, 2026. Outlet displayed gaps of $55.01 and $106.00 for the same $43.99 basket.

Site speed analysis12 / 52

Two focused changes for the first speed pass

01

Prioritize the main image and reduce oversized downloads

The homepage LCP image uses lazy loading and automatic priority. Load that first-screen image eagerly, give it high priority, and keep below-fold media lazy-loaded.

Review responsive image sizes and compression. PageSpeed estimates 537 KiB in potential homepage image savings.

02

Trace the PDP’s script and rendering work

The PDP records 480 ms of blocking time and 12 long tasks. Identify the responsible theme or app work before changing scripts.

Defer nonessential work only after confirming that gallery, variants, and cart behavior remain intact.

After changes, repeat the same mobile tests several times and compare medians. Preserve image quality and verify the shopping journey.

Homepage diagnostics · Product diagnostics · Estimated savings are diagnostic opportunities, not guaranteed gains.

Homepage CRO actions14 / 52

A hero that names the assortment

H1High priority

Opportunity

The broad shopping CTA leaves visitors to find their own route through the catalog.

Recommended change

  • Name Harmony Kingdom and Polish Pottery in the supporting copy.
  • Offer two direct collection CTAs; place USP icons beneath them.
  • On mobile, lead with the image, then the title and buttons.

Why it mattersShoppers can recognize the offer and choose a relevant starting point.

Reference: Polish Pottery Outlet; Fitzula’s

Homepage CRO actions15 / 52

Shipping reassurance before product browsing

H2High priority

Opportunity

Shipping benefits and dispatch timing can be more prominent at the first shopping decision.

Recommended change

  • State “Free US shipping on orders $100+” in the announcement.
  • Repeat careful packing and dispatch within two business days.
  • Keep eligibility consistent: US Ground Advantage, after discounts and before tax.

Why it mattersDelivery expectations become clear before a shopper commits to a product.

Reference: Replacements’ delivery clarity

Homepage CRO actions16 / 52

Visible search for collectors who know the item

H3High priority

Opportunity

Search currently begins with a header icon.

Recommended change

  • Expose a search field on desktop and below the mobile header.
  • Support piece names, makers, patterns and product codes.
  • Verify known queries against the actual catalog.

Why it mattersExact-item shoppers can begin their task immediately.

Reference: Replacements; Polish Pottery Outlet

Homepage CRO actions17 / 52

Category tiles that explain where to shop

Opportunity

The existing category tiles can work harder as a clear shopping menu.

Product page CRO actions24 / 52

Make the item and purchase action easy to scan

P1High priority

Opportunity

Long titles combine several identifiers and push the purchase controls down.

Recommended change

  • Give Add to Bag the strongest visual emphasis.
  • On mobile, show a compact sticky purchase bar after the main controls leave view.

Why it mattersShoppers can identify the piece and find the purchase action faster.

Reference: Replacements’ structured product identity

Product page CRO actions25 / 52

Keep essential facts directly below the price

P2High priority

Opportunity

Detailed information exists, but its placement and structure vary by product.

Recommended change

  • Place Made in and Material immediately under the price.
  • Summarize condition, dimensions and category-specific facts nearby.
  • Use accordions for full specifications, care and provenance; hide unknown fields.

Why it mattersThe details needed to assess suitability are visible at the decision point.

Reference: Replacements; Fitzula’s; Polish Pottery House

Product page CRO actions26 / 52

Use the gallery to answer item-specific questions

P3High priority

Opportunity

Collectible buyers need to judge condition, markings and what is included.

Recommended change

  • Include base marks, interiors, flaws and accompanying materials when relevant.
  • Keep thumbnails and zoom accessible; use actual-item photography when claimed.

Why it mattersGood visual evidence reduces uncertainty that copy alone cannot resolve.

Product page CRO actions27 / 52

Explain delivery and show care in packing

P4High priority

Opportunity

Delivery and return details should be visible beside the purchase controls.

Recommended change

  • Show the applicable shipping threshold and two-business-day dispatch.
  • Keep the 14-day request window linked to return eligibility and exclusions.
  • Add a careful-packing banner below the main product area.

Why it mattersFragile-item buyers can judge service expectations before adding to the bag.

Reference: Polish Pottery House; Replacements

Product page CRO actions28 / 52

Make availability match the actual inventory

P5High priority

Opportunity

Unique collectibles and repeatable pottery need different quantity behavior.

Recommended change

  • Show a plain, accurate availability state.
  • Limit quantity to actual stock; disable impossible increases.
  • Explain update failures beside the control and keep the selected quantity.

Why it mattersThe interface avoids promising stock that cannot be purchased.

Reference: Replacements’ purchase clarity

Product page CRO actions29 / 52

Give sold pieces a useful next step

P6Medium priority

Opportunity

Sold listings still help collectors research a piece, but cannot complete a purchase.

Recommended change

  • Replace the purchase action with a route to available pieces.
  • Avoid restock promises for unique stock unless they can be fulfilled.

Why it mattersResearch traffic gets a relevant way to continue shopping.

Reference: Avoid unavailable-product dead ends seen in competitor merchandising

Product page CRO actions30 / 52

Recommend pieces through meaningful relationships

Opportunity

Related products should provide a useful alternative or complement.

Why it mattersA relevant next choice is more useful than a generic product carousel.

Cart page CRO actions43 / 52

Let shoppers review the order without leaving the page

D1Foundation priority

Opportunity

The existing add confirmation does not provide a complete editable order summary.

Recommended change

  • Open the drawer after a successful add and from the header bag control.
  • Show all line items, shipping progress, subtotal and Checkout.
  • Use an obvious close control; support Escape, focus return and an empty state.

Why it mattersCustomers can review the order while keeping their browsing context.

Reference: Polish Pottery House’s editable drawer

Cart page CRO actions44 / 52

Show one accurate free-shipping calculation

D2High priority

Opportunity

The inspected cart did not show the remaining spend for the published offer.

Recommended change

  • Calculate the exact gap to the $100 merchandise threshold.
  • Use the qualifying subtotal after discounts and before tax.
  • Update after every edit; switch to a qualification message at $100.

Why it mattersShoppers understand the offer and can trust that every amount agrees.

Reference: Replacements; avoid Outlet’s conflicting threshold messages

Cart page CRO actions45 / 52

Distinguish subtotal from the final charge

D3High priority

Opportunity

The current cart calls the merchandise amount an estimated total while other costs remain open.

Recommended change

  • Label the merchandise amount “Subtotal”.
  • Below $100, explain that shipping and tax are calculated at checkout.
  • When eligible, state free US Ground Advantage shipping and keep the tax note.

Why it mattersThe amount shown has a clear meaning before checkout.

Reference: Replacements’ cost breakdown; Fitzula’s shipping clarity

Cart page CRO actions46 / 52

Keep cart edits simple and inventory-aware

D4High priority

Opportunity

Quantity and removal functions need to carry into the drawer.

Recommended change

Why it mattersCustomers can correct the order without restarting their journey.

Reference: Polish Pottery House; Replacements

Cart page CRO actions47 / 52

Summary & next steps50 / 52

Build the purchase essentials first

StageDeliverablesCompletion condition
1 · Purchase essentialsHero, search and available products; P1–P5; C1–C4; cart costs and shippingA shopper can find an available piece, understand it and see the purchase conditions.
2 · Complete the journeyDrawer editing and checkout; sold-piece alternatives; product help; Our Story and collection contextBrowsing, order review, reassurance and recovery work together on mobile and desktop.
3 · Extend discoveryGift routes, email updates and curated related-product / cart recommendationsUseful stock groups and a maintenance routine support each feature.

Build shared product fields and shipping messages once. Reuse them across templates so the experience stays consistent.

Summary & next steps51 / 52

Check the complete journey before release

AreaAcceptance checks
Product informationReview Unbearables, a new pottery item, a sold piece and a listing with missing optional data. Verify origin, material, condition and included materials.
BrowsingTest search by name/code, combined filters, no results, sorting, Load More and browser Back. Confirm stock states across the full collection.
Cart and checkoutAdd, remove and edit items; handle failed updates and stock limits. Check $99.99, exactly $100 and discounts that remove eligibility.
Mobile and accessibilityCheck hero order, gallery, sticky purchase controls, drawer scrolling, keyboard focus and readable text at zoom.
PerformanceRepeat mobile PageSpeed runs after changes; compare medians and confirm the gallery, cart and checkout still work.

Implement and review in an unpublished theme preview, then publish the verified version and retain a rollback copy.

Summary & next steps52 / 52

Measure direction without over-reading a small sample

At release

  • Record the launch date and the changes made.
  • Verify Online Store funnel tracking and review internal preview traffic.
  • Confirm shipping rules, availability and product fields match the live catalog.

After release

  • Review website sessions, add-to-cart, checkout reach and completed orders separately from marketplaces.
  • Track counts alongside rates; investigate errors and recurring shopper questions.
  • Revisit progress after four to six weeks, allowing more time if volume remains low.

Success starts with a clearer, dependable buying journey. The current sample does not support a reliable A/B test, conversion-uplift promise or revenue forecast.
